- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast peak heights.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast peaks at 1–2% below true high.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-horizon, model delays response — adjust forecast downward early in that shift.
- Model underestimates true volatility in late horizon (e.g., 25–30 days) when sentiment is mixed — add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to final 5–10 days.
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% in last 3–5 days, model is lagging — apply 1–2% upward correction to next forecast window.
- When sentiment history shows alternating +/– patterns, model tends to average out — avoid smoothing; preserve recent sentiment-driven momentum.
